requirements.quote:
Once the handshake is confirmed (see Section 4.1.2), an endpoint MAY
   initiate a key update.
requirements.condition: Once the endpoint's handshake is confirmed.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the endpoint to initiate a key update.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not initiate a key update before handshake confirmation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can request key updates before and after the handshake-confirmed transition and inspect whether update packets are emitted.

requirements.quote:
The Key Phase bit indicates which packet protection keys are used to
   protect the packet.
requirements.condition: For each 1-RTT packet protected under a packet-protection key generation.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Key Phase bit to identify the key generation used to protect that packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not emit a Key Phase bit value inconsistent with the keys that protect the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet's Key Phase value can be compared with the key generation that successfully authenticates and decrypts it.

requirements.quote:
The Key Phase bit is initially set to 0 for the
   first set of 1-RTT packets
requirements.condition: For the first set of 1-RTT packets sent before any key update.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Key Phase bit to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set the initial Key Phase bit to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The first emitted 1-RTT packets can be decrypted and their unprotected Key Phase bits inspected.

requirements.quote:
The Key Phase bit is initially set to 0 for the
   first set of 1-RTT packets and toggled to signal each subsequent key
   update.
requirements.condition: For each key update after the initial 1-RTT key generation.
requirements.required_behavior: Toggle the Key Phase bit relative to the preceding key generation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain the preceding Key Phase value when switching to the next key generation.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces across successive key updates can verify alternating Key Phase values for adjacent key generations.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that notices a changed Key Phase bit updates
   keys and decrypts the packet that contains the changed value.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a packet whose Key Phase bit differs from the currently used phase.
requirements.required_behavior: Update the packet-protection keys for the changed phase.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue using only the previous receive keys after detecting the changed Key Phase.
requirements.why_checkable: Key-schedule instrumentation can verify that detection of the changed phase invokes derivation or installation of the next keys.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that notices a changed Key Phase bit updates
   keys and decrypts the packet that contains the changed value.
requirements.condition: After an endpoint notices a changed Key Phase bit and updates its keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Decrypt the packet containing the changed Key Phase value using the corresponding updated keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard an otherwise valid phase-changing packet without attempting decryption using the updated keys.
requirements.why_checkable: A valid first packet from the next key phase can be delivered and observed for successful decryption and frame processing.

requirements.quote: Initiating a key update results in both endpoints updating keys.
requirements.condition: When either endpoint initiates a QUIC key update.
requirements.required_behavior: Cause both endpoints to transition to the updated key generation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave either endpoint permanently using only the preceding key generation.
requirements.why_checkable: After one peer initiates an update, bidirectional traffic can verify that both peers install and use the corresponding updated keys.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints
   MUST NOT send a TLS KeyUpdate message.
requirements.condition: During a QUIC connection, including when updating packet-protection keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the QUIC Key Phase mechanism rather than a TLS KeyUpdate message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send any TLS KeyUpdate message.
requirements.why_checkable: Decrypted TLS handshake-message traces carried by QUIC can be checked for the absence of KeyUpdate messages.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MUST treat the
   receipt of a TLS KeyUpdate message as a connection error of type
   0x010a, equivalent to a fatal TLS alert of unexpected_message; see
   Section 4.8.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a TLS KeyUpdate message over QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the event as a connection error of type 0x010a.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or process the TLS KeyUpdate as a valid QUIC key update.
requirements.error_behavior: Close the connection with error code 0x010a, corresponding to the fatal TLS alert unexpected_message.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can inject a TLS KeyUpdate message and verify the resulting connection-close code and absence of a successful key transition.
